answer: Each identity posts a 50-credit bond and tags each output with a nectar mark from key and inputs. A lotus auditor re-runs a sample; a copied or non-reproducing output burns the bond. A nadir audit re-runs the full input set when patterns match, so outputs cannot be pre-shaped for a shallow sample. Copying output across fakes costs 90 each, with a shared-pattern surcharge, so the k-th fake costs 90+5(k-1) and 1,000 lock 2,587,500. A rented output farm fails because each nectar mark binds one key to one input set. An honest agent pays one 40 fee and recovers its bond on a pass.
